Old Testament.name: Pentateuch
Old Testament.description: The first five books (Torah) providing the law and the history of creation through the death of Moses.

Old Testament.name: Historical Books
Old Testament.description: Twelve books narrating Israel's entry into the Promised Land, the rise and fall of its kingdoms, and the return from exile.

Old Testament.name: Wisdom Literature
Old Testament.description: Five books of poetry, songs, and proverbs exploring human experience and godly living.

Old Testament.name: Major Prophets
Old Testament.description: Longer prophetic works containing messages of judgment and Messianic hope; named 'Major' for their length.

Old Testament.name: Minor Prophets
Old Testament.description: Twelve shorter prophetic books addressing social justice, repentance, and the 'Day of the Lord'.

New Testament.name: Gospels
New Testament.description: Four accounts of the life, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ.

New Testament.name: Church History
New Testament.description: A single book (Acts) documenting the birth of the early church and the spread of the Gospel.

New Testament.name: Pauline Epistles
New Testament.description: Thirteen letters written by the Apostle Paul to specific churches or individuals regarding doctrine and conduct.

New Testament.name: General Epistles
New Testament.description: Seven letters by various authors (Peter, James, John, Jude) written to the broader Christian community.

New Testament.name: Apocalyptic Literature
New Testament.description: The final book (Revelation) using symbolic visions to reveal Christ's ultimate victory and the new creation.

books.name: Genesis
books.author: Moses
books.explanation: The book of beginnings. Covers the Creation, the Fall of man, Noah’s Flood, the Tower of Babel, and the lives of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph.

chapterDescription.description: The creation of the world; God creates light, sky, land, plants, stars, fish, birds, animals, and man.
The first Sabbath; the formation of man; the Garden of Eden; the creation of woman.
The serpent's deception; the fall of man; the curse and the expulsion from Eden.
Cain and Abel; the first murder; the lineage of Cain and the birth of Seth.
The genealogy from Adam to Noah, documenting the ages and deaths of the patriarchs.
The wickedness of the world; God instructs Noah to build an ark to survive the flood.
Noah and his family enter the ark; the Great Flood covers the entire earth.
The waters recede; Noah sends out a raven and a dove; the ark rests on Ararat; God's covenant.
God blesses Noah; the rainbow as a covenant sign; Noah's vineyard and his sons.
The Table of Nations; the descendants of Noah's sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The Tower of Babel and the confusion of languages; the lineage of Shem to Abram.
The call of Abram; God's promise; Abram and Sarai in Egypt.
Abram and Lot separate; Lot chooses the plain of Jordan; God renews the promise to Abram.
The war of the kings; Lot is captured and rescued by Abram; Melchizedek blesses Abram.
God's formal covenant with Abram; the promise of an heir and the land of Canaan.
Sarai gives Hagar to Abram; the birth of Ishmael; Hagar's encounter with the angel.
The covenant of circumcision; Abram renamed Abraham; Sarai renamed Sarah; Isaac promised.
Three angels visit Abraham; Sarah's laughter; Abraham intercedes for Sodom.
The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot's escape; the origin of Moab and Ammon.
Abraham and Sarah at Gerar; Abimelech is warned by God in a dream.
The birth of Isaac; Hagar and Ishmael sent away; Abraham's treaty with Abimelech.
The testing of Abraham; the commanded sacrifice of Isaac and God's provision of a ram.
The death of Sarah; Abraham purchases the cave of Machpelah for a burial place.
Abraham's servant seeks a wife for Isaac; Rebekah is chosen and brought to Isaac.
Abraham's death; Ishmael's descendants; the birth of Jacob and Esau; Esau sells his birthright.
Isaac dwells in Gerar; God's promise to Isaac; Isaac's prosperity and his treaty with Abimelech.
Jacob deceives Isaac to receive Esau's blessing; Esau's anger and Jacob's flight.
Jacob's ladder; God's promise at Bethel; Jacob's vow to God.
Jacob arrives in Padan-aram; he works for Laban to marry Rachel but is given Leah.
The birth of Jacob’s sons; Jacob’s cleverness in increasing his flocks.
Jacob flees from Laban; Rachel steals the household idols; Laban pursues and makes a covenant.
Jacob prepares to meet Esau; he wrestles with an angel and his name is changed to Israel.
The reconciliation of Jacob and Esau; Jacob settles in Succoth and Shechem.
The defilement of Dinah; the revenge of Simeon and Levi against the Shechemites.
Jacob returns to Bethel; death of Rachel and Isaac; the twelve sons of Jacob.
The genealogy of Esau and the rulers of Edom.
Joseph’s dreams; his brothers sell him into slavery; Joseph is taken to Egypt.
The story of Judah and Tamar; the birth of Perez and Zerah.
Joseph in Potiphar's house; he is falsely accused and cast into prison.
Joseph interprets the dreams of the butler and the baker in prison.
Pharaoh’s dreams; Joseph's interpretation; Joseph is promoted to ruler of Egypt.
The brothers of Joseph go to Egypt to buy grain; Joseph recognizes them.
The second journey to Egypt with Benjamin; Joseph feasts with his brothers.
Joseph’s silver cup is found in Benjamin’s sack; Judah’s plea for Benjamin.
Joseph reveals himself to his brothers; he sends for Jacob to come to Egypt.
Jacob and his family migrate to Egypt; the meeting of Jacob and Joseph.
Jacob’s family settles in Goshen; Joseph manages the famine; Jacob’s final request.
Jacob blesses Joseph’s sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.
Jacob’s prophetic blessings for his twelve sons; the death of Jacob.
The burial of Jacob; Joseph’s reassurance to his brothers; the death of Joseph.

books.name: Exodus
books.author: Moses
books.explanation: God delivers Israel from slavery. Key events: The birth of Moses, the burning bush, the Ten Plagues of Egypt, the crossing of the Red Sea, and the giving of the Ten Commandments at Sinai.
books.explanation-ext: God saves Israel from slavery in Egypt, and then enters into a special relationship with them.

books.name: Leviticus
books.author: Moses
books.explanation: A handbook for priests and a guide for holy living. It details the sacrificial system, dietary laws, and the Day of Atonement rituals.

books.name: Numbers
books.author: Moses
books.explanation: Records the census of Israel and their 40 years of wandering in the wilderness due to their lack of faith. Includes the story of the bronze serpent and Balaam’s donkey.

books.name: Deuteronomy
books.author: Moses
books.explanation: Moses’ final sermons to a new generation. He repeats the Law, calls for total devotion to God, and dies on Mount Nebo before Israel enters the Promised Land.

books.name: Joshua
books.author: Joshua
books.explanation: The conquest of Canaan. Key events: The fall of Jericho, the sun standing still, and the division of the land among the twelve tribes.

books.name: Judges
books.author: Samuel (traditionally)
books.explanation: The period before the kings where 'everyone did what was right in his own eyes.' Features the stories of Deborah, Gideon, and Samson’s strength.

books.name: Ruth
books.author: Samuel (traditionally)
books.explanation: A story of loyalty during the time of the Judges. Ruth, a Moabite widow, chooses to follow God and becomes the great-grandmother of King David.

books.name: 1 Samuel
books.author: Samuel, Nathan, Gad
books.explanation: The transition from judges to monarchy. Includes Samuel’s call, the rise and fall of King Saul, and the famous battle of David and Goliath.

books.name: 2 Samuel
books.author: Nathan, Gad
books.explanation: The story of David’s reign as king. Covers the establishment of Jerusalem, the Davidic Covenant, and David’s sin with Bathsheba.

books.name: 1 Kings
books.author: Jeremiah (traditionally)
books.explanation: The peak and decline of the kingdom. Covers Solomon’s wisdom, the building of the Temple, and the division into Israel (North) and Judah (South).

books.name: 2 Kings
books.author: Jeremiah (traditionally)
books.explanation: The downfall of both kingdoms. Features the miracles of Elisha and the eventual exile of Israel to Assyria and Judah to Babylon.

books.name: 1 Chronicles
books.author: Ezra (traditionally)
books.explanation: A priestly perspective on history. Focuses on the genealogies from Adam and the spiritual highlights of David’s preparations for the Temple.

books.name: 2 Chronicles
books.author: Ezra (traditionally)
books.explanation: Continues the history from Solomon to the decree of Cyrus, focusing on the kings of Judah and their spiritual reforms.

books.name: Ezra
books.author: Ezra
books.explanation: The return of the Jews from exile. Covers the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem and Ezra’s work in teaching the Law.

books.name: Nehemiah
books.author: Nehemiah
books.explanation: Nehemiah leads the effort to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem in just 52 days and institutes social and religious reforms.

books.name: Esther
books.author: Unknown
books.explanation: A Jewish girl becomes Queen of Persia and risks her life to save her people from a plot by Haman. Origin of the feast of Purim.

books.name: Job
books.author: Unknown
books.explanation: A poetic drama exploring why the righteous suffer. Job loses everything but remains faithful, eventually encountering God’s majesty.

books.name: Psalms
books.author: David, others
books.explanation: A collection of 150 poems, songs, and prayers. Many were written by David during his life as a shepherd, fugitive, and king.

books.name: Proverbs
books.author: Solomon, others
books.explanation: Practical wisdom for daily life. Themes include the fear of God, the value of hard work, and the dangers of foolishness.

books.name: Ecclesiastes
books.author: Solomon
books.explanation: A philosophical search for the meaning of life. The author concludes that everything is 'vanity' without a proper relationship with God.

books.name: Song of Solomon
books.author: Solomon
books.explanation: A poetic celebration of the love between a bridegroom and his bride, symbolizing God’s love for His people.

books.name: Isaiah
books.author: Isaiah
books.explanation: The 'Prince of Prophets.' Contains powerful prophecies of judgment and comfort, specifically predicting the birth and suffering of the Messiah.

books.name: Jeremiah
books.author: Jeremiah
books.explanation: The weeping prophet. He warned Judah of the coming Babylonian destruction and promised a New Covenant where God's law is written on the heart.

books.name: Lamentations
books.author: Jeremiah
books.explanation: Five poems mourning the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple by the Babylonians.

books.name: Ezekiel
books.author: Ezekiel
books.explanation: Prophecies given while in exile. Known for vivid visions, like the valley of dry bones coming to life and the glory of God leaving the Temple.

books.name: Daniel
books.author: Daniel
books.explanation: Faithfulness in a foreign land. Stories include the fiery furnace, the lions’ den, and apocalyptic visions of future world empires.

books.name: Hosea
books.author: Hosea
books.explanation: Hosea is told to marry an unfaithful wife as a living parable of God’s heartbreaking love for an unfaithful Israel.

books.name: Joel
books.author: Joel
books.explanation: Uses a devastating locust plague as a warning of the coming 'Day of the Lord' and promises the future outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

books.name: Amos
books.author: Amos
books.explanation: A shepherd-prophet who rebuked the northern kingdom for social injustice, religious hypocrisy, and the oppression of the poor.

books.name: Obadiah
books.author: Obadiah
books.explanation: A short prophecy against the nation of Edom for their pride and their gloating over the downfall of Jerusalem.

books.name: Jonah
books.author: Jonah
books.explanation: A reluctant prophet is swallowed by a great fish while fleeing God's call to preach repentance to the enemy city of Nineveh.

books.name: Micah
books.author: Micah
books.explanation: Predicts the birth of the Messiah in Bethlehem and calls for people to 'do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.'

books.name: Nahum
books.author: Nahum
books.explanation: A prophecy of the certain and final destruction of Nineveh, the capital of the cruel Assyrian empire.

books.name: Habakkuk
books.author: Habakkuk
books.explanation: A dialogue where the prophet questions why God uses the wicked Babylonians to judge Judah. It ends with a song of total trust in God.

books.name: Zephaniah
books.author: Zephaniah
books.explanation: Warns that the Day of the Lord is near for all nations, but promises that God will rejoice over a repentant remnant with singing.

books.name: Haggai
books.author: Haggai
books.explanation: A direct challenge to the returning exiles to stop focusing on their own houses and finish rebuilding God’s Temple.

books.name: Zechariah
books.author: Zechariah
books.explanation: Encouragement for the Temple builders through visions and prophecies of the Messiah’s entry into Jerusalem on a donkey.

books.name: Malachi
books.author: Malachi
books.explanation: The final message of the Old Testament. Rebukes the people for spiritual apathy and promises the coming of a messenger (John the Baptist).

books.name: Matthew
books.author: Matthew
books.explanation: Presents Jesus as the Messiah-King. Features the Sermon on the Mount and many parables of the Kingdom, like the Sower and the Hidden Treasure.
books.description: Traditionally attributed to Matthew (Levi), the tax collector and one of the 12 apostles. Scholars generally believe the author was a Jewish Christian writing for a similar audience, likely using Mark as a source.

books.name: Mark
books.author: John Mark
books.explanation: The shortest Gospel, focusing on Jesus as the Suffering Servant. It emphasizes Jesus’ actions and miracles over His long discourses.
books.description: Traditionally attributed to John Mark, a companion of the Apostle Peter. It is believed to be the first Gospel written (c. 70 AD) and likely reflects Peter's testimonies.

books.name: Luke
books.author: Luke
books.explanation: The most detailed Gospel. Contains unique parables like the Good Samaritan and the Prodigal Son, emphasizing Jesus’ concern for the outcast.
books.description: Traditionally attributed to Luke, a Gentile physician and traveling companion of the Apostle Paul. The author also wrote the Book of Acts.

books.name: John
books.author: John (Apostle)
books.explanation: Focuses on the deity of Jesus through seven 'I Am' statements and seven signs. It includes the famous conversation with Nicodemus (John 3).
books.description: Traditionally attributed to John, the 'beloved disciple' and one of the 12 apostles. It is considered the latest Gospel (c. 90–100 AD) and differs significantly from the other three.

books.name: Acts
books.author: Luke
books.explanation: The history of the early church. Key events: Pentecost, the conversion of Paul, and the spread of the Gospel from Jerusalem to Rome.

books.name: Romans
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Paul’s masterpiece on theology, explaining how both Jews and Gentiles are justified by faith in Christ rather than by the Law.

books.name: 1 Corinthians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: A letter addressing problems in the Corinthian church, including divisions, lawsuits, and spiritual gifts. Contains the 'Love Chapter' (Ch. 13).

books.name: 2 Corinthians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Paul defends his apostolic authority and shares the nature of true ministry, which is often carried out in weakness and suffering.

books.name: Galatians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: A passionate defense of Christian liberty against those who said believers must still follow Jewish ceremonial laws to be saved.

books.name: Ephesians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Explains the believer's position in Christ and the armor of God. Focuses on the unity of the church as the body of Christ.

books.name: Philippians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: The 'Epistle of Joy,' written from prison. Paul encourages the church to have the same humble mind as Christ.

books.name: Colossians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Combats false teachings by exalting the absolute supremacy and sufficiency of Jesus Christ over all other powers.

books.name: 1 Thessalonians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Encouragement for a young church facing persecution. Provides the clearest teaching on the return of Christ and the 'Rapture'.

books.name: 2 Thessalonians
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Clarifies misunderstandings about the Day of the Lord and warns against idleness while waiting for Christ’s return.

books.name: 1 Timothy
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: A 'Pastoral Epistle' giving Timothy instructions on church leadership, the qualifications for elders, and sound doctrine.

books.name: 2 Timothy
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Paul’s final letter before his execution. He encourages Timothy to 'preach the word' and remain faithful until the end.

books.name: Titus
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: Guidance for Titus on the island of Crete regarding church organization and the importance of teaching believers to do good works.

books.name: Philemon
books.author: Paul
books.explanation: A personal appeal to a slave owner to receive his runaway slave, Onesimus, back not as a slave, but as a brother in Christ.

books.name: Hebrews
books.author: Unknown
books.explanation: Shows that Jesus is superior to angels, Moses, and the old sacrificial system. Includes the 'Hall of Faith' in Chapter 11.

books.name: James
books.author: James
books.explanation: A practical guide to Christian ethics, famously teaching that 'faith without works is dead.'

books.name: 1 Peter
books.author: Peter
books.explanation: A letter of hope for Christians scattered and suffering under Roman persecution, calling them to live as 'elect exiles.'

books.name: 2 Peter
books.author: Peter
books.explanation: A warning against false teachers who deny the second coming of Christ. It affirms the reliability of the Scriptures.

books.name: 1 John
books.author: John (Apostle)
books.explanation: Writes to give believers assurance of their salvation based on their love for others and their belief that Jesus is the Son of God.

books.name: 2 John
books.author: John (Apostle)
books.explanation: A brief warning to a local church to walk in the truth and not to show hospitality to false teachers who deny Christ.

books.name: 3 John
books.author: John (Apostle)
books.explanation: A personal letter to Gaius, praising him for his hospitality and warning against a proud leader named Diotrephes.

books.name: Jude
books.author: Jude
books.explanation: A short, urgent call to 'contend for the faith' against godless men who have slipped into the church unnoticed.

books.name: Revelation
books.author: John (Apostle)
books.explanation: An apocalyptic vision of the spiritual war between good and evil, the return of Christ, and the creation of a New Heaven and New Earth.
